documents.unit: AI at Amherst (Academic Technology Services / IT)
documents.title: Updated AI Usage Guidelines
documents.summary: A short January 2026 community-wide guideline that welcomes responsible AI exploration and sets conditions: human verification, privacy and data-classification limits, vetting of tools through AskIT, and encouraged (not required) transparency. It is written mainly for employees and says almost nothing specific about student coursework or course-level rules.
documents.stance_why: The document says "We encourage thoughtful, responsible exploration of AI" and lets members "generate ideas, drafts, and analyses, provided that" conditions are met. It sets no ban and no per-course delegation, so AI is allowed with conditions: permit rather than encourage, because the welcome is paired with firm verification and privacy limits.

units.why: Opening framing says Amherst "recognizes that generative AI is rapidly reshaping" learning, teaching and work, which is a statement of context and purpose, so it is general, informational, and best fits the institution-level framework type.
units.anchor: generative AI is rapidly reshaping the ways we learn, teach, and work
units.frag_start: Amherst College recognizes that generative AI

units.why: "We encourage thoughtful, responsible exploration of AI" is the default position of the college: AI exploration is welcomed, so it is a permit/encourage default (P02) rather than a framework statement.
units.anchor: We encourage thoughtful, responsible exploration of AI
units.frag_end: how we operate as a community

units.why: "we remain committed to protecting privacy, maintaining accuracy, and upholding the academic and institutional integrity" states the principles bounding AI use; it is a principle statement for the institution, so P56 fits better than a specific privacy or verification rule.
units.anchor: committed to protecting privacy, maintaining accuracy, and upholding the academic and institutional integrity
units.frag_start: At the same time, we remain

units.why: "apply to all members of the Amherst community" defines scope: who is covered. It is a scope statement, so P61 (define the policy's scope) fits, while P56 is for purposes and principles.
units.anchor: These guidelines apply to all members of the Amherst community

units.why: "Users are responsible for the accuracy and integrity of any material they create... that was generated or assisted by AI" makes users answerable for what they submit or distribute, so it is a must-level ownership rule (P29); verification is covered separately in other units.
units.anchor: Users are responsible for the accuracy and integrity of any material they create
units.frag_start: Users are responsible for the accuracy

units.why: "All final decisions, publications, and communications remain the responsibility of the human author or decision-maker" keeps the human as the decision-maker so AI does not replace human judgment; this is P32 rather than P29 because it concerns decision authority, not ownership of output.
units.anchor: remain the responsibility of the human author or decision-maker

units.why: "may use these tools to generate ideas, drafts, and analyses, provided that" is a conditional permission for brainstorming, drafting and analysis. The closest type is brainstorming and idea generation (P15); it does not fit P16 because it is not specifically about code.
units.anchor: may use these tools to generate ideas, drafts, and analyses, provided that

units.why: The first condition, "All data used are appropriate for public or internal sharing", limits what data can be put into AI tools, so it is a data-protection rule (P50), not a ban on uploading course materials (P49).
units.anchor: All data used are appropriate for public or internal sharing

units.why: "reviewed and verified by a person before being distributed or published" requires human checking of AI output before it goes out. This is verification (P31), a must-level condition on the permission.
units.anchor: Any AI-generated material is reviewed and verified by a person before being distributed or published

units.why: "The use of AI aligns with applicable academic, professional, and ethical standards, including the Student Code of Conduct" ties AI use to existing conduct rules, so AI is handled under existing rules. P45 (existing rules) is closer than P36 because the text does not itself call AI misuse misconduct.
units.anchor: The use of AI aligns with applicable academic, professional, and ethical standards

units.why: "These resources will be updated as appropriate as guidance changes" says the linked guidance is provisional and will be revised, so it is a revisit-regularly statement (P54).
units.anchor: These resources will be updated as appropriate as guidance changes

units.why: "do not include sensitive, confidential, or personally identifiable information (PII) in any prompt or upload" is a direct prohibition on entering personal or confidential data, so it is a protect-personal-data rule (P50), must-not, restricting.
units.anchor: do not include sensitive, confidential, or personally identifiable information (PII) in any prompt or upload

units.why: "Many AI tools do not provide robust privacy or data controls" is a factual warning that tools store or use data, and it justifies the data rule. It is informational, and fits P50 (tools store prompts).
units.anchor: Many AI tools do not provide robust privacy or data controls

units.why: "student or personnel records (such as transcripts, evaluations, or tenure materials)" lists examples of data that must not be given to AI; it specifies the protected categories (including student records) under the same data-protection rule, so P50.
units.anchor: student or personnel records (such as transcripts, evaluations, or tenure materials)

units.why: "treat all internal information as non-shareable with AI tools unless confirmed otherwise" sets a default-deny rule for internal information, a data-protection rule (P50), with should-level wording ("When in doubt").
units.anchor: treat all internal information as non-shareable with AI tools unless confirmed otherwise

units.why: "Internal (Purple) or Shareable (Green) should be entered into college-licensed AI tools only" restricts data of these classes to licensed tools, so it directs users to vetted tools (P50) and is addressed to employees ("employees should consult").
units.anchor: should be entered into college-licensed AI tools only

units.why: "Data classified as Sensitive (Yellow) may be used with college-licensed AI tools following review and approval by AskIT" sets a conditional permission for sensitive data tied to review; it is a vetted-tools and data rule (P50), with may modality.
units.anchor: may be used with college-licensed AI tools following review and approval by AskIT

units.why: "consult AskIT to confirm that appropriate privacy, security, and risk assessments have been completed" before adopting AI tools or features is a vetting requirement for tools; it is closest to prefer-vetted-tools (P50), and it differs from P65 because it addresses users, not institutional contract review.
units.anchor: Before adopting new AI tools or enabling AI features within existing platforms, consult
units.policy: Before adopting new AI tools or enabling AI features within existing platforms, consult AskIT to confirm that appropriate privacy, security, and risk assessments have been completed.

units.why: "Do not use College data in any manner which may lead to its use in model training or fine-tuning" forbids use that would train models on college data; it concerns data/IP exposure, and P50 fits better than P52 because no ownership or licensing question is addressed.
units.anchor: Do not use College data in any manner which may lead to

units.why: "Generative AI systems can be inaccurate, inconsistent, or biased" warns that output may be wrong or biased, and the next sentence tells users to check it. This unit is the warning, and P31 (AI output can be wrong) fits it.
units.anchor: Generative AI systems can be inaccurate, inconsistent, or biased

units.why: "Always review and fact-check their suggestions, particularly in technical, academic, or policy-related work" commands verification of AI suggestions, a must-level verify rule (P31).
units.anchor: Always review and fact-check their suggestions, particularly in technical, academic, or policy-related work

units.why: "Users are responsible for the accuracy and integrity of any material, code, or workflows they create" repeats the responsibility rule but adds code and workflows. It is not an exact repeat, so I code it as ownership of everything submitted or distributed (P29).
units.anchor: accuracy and integrity of any material, code, or workflows they create
units.frag_start: Users are responsible for the accuracy

units.why: "transparency is encouraged" when AI plays a significant role in a work is a soft, recommended disclosure, not a requirement, so it is P24 with should modality and permit stance.
units.anchor: Clearly indicating that AI contributed to a piece of work

units.why: "contact AskIT" for technical, privacy or security questions or to request a review of a new AI tool is a support/procedure statement. No type covers help-desk routing exactly, and the nearest, P50 (vetted tools), is about data protection, so it is UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: or to request a review of a new AI tool, contact
units.uncovered_note: Names a support contact (AskIT) for technical, privacy and security questions and for requesting review of a new AI tool.

notes: Single university-level document; employee-oriented and nearly silent on student coursework. No school or computing layer found; course layer deferred in collect file. The Task Force report PDF was inaccessible.
